name: Roasted Parsnip & Thyme Soup
why: Parsnips are at their sweetest right now, after the first frosts — roasting before blending is the trick that takes a plain root soup into something deep and nutty. Hands-off oven time makes it an easy weeknight comfort classic.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1/2 tsp dried)
1/2 cup heavy cream or coconut milk (optional)

steps: Peel and chop the parsnips into 1-inch chunks.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Toss the parsnips with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden, turning halfway through.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the roasted parsnips and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend with an immersion blender (or in batches) until completely smooth.
Stir in the cream or coconut milk if using; adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Heat gently until warmed through — don't let it boil.
Serve in warm bowls, garnished with fresh thyme sprigs.

pro_tips: Roasting the parsnips first is the whole trick — the Maillard browning adds a nutty, almost caramel depth that boiled parsnips never get.
Let the soup cool slightly before blending — it purées smoother and you avoid a hot mess in the blender lid.
